clue.text: Cleaned up and tied the knot, without a bean

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the wedding word goes round the money

parts.note: to tie the knot is to marry, so wed
a means one, the Roman numeral I
a bean is slang for a coin, here a penny, abbreviated P

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up and gets married while completely broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a bean' reads as the idiom for penniless, but 'without' is a container signal (outside) and 'a bean' is one penny, IP.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe something is to clean it with a cloth, so wiped describes a surface cleaned up.

clue.text: Determination is certain to? Might

parts.note: will expresses certainty about the future
might means strength or power

explanation.surface: A puzzled thought: is resolve sure to win? Perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like the verb of possibility, but is the noun, strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength of mind or resolve is a synonym.

clue.text: Infernal ruler with pipe under bed

explanation.surface: The lord of hell smokes his pipe below the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUTO also named the Second World War fuel line, Pipe-Line Under The Ocean, laid on the Channel seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto ruled the classical underworld; the wartime fuel pipe ran along the sea floor.

clue.text: Reckless speed possibly leading to rebuke

indicators.note: leading to puts the scrambled letters before the next part
possibly signals one of the possible arrangements of the letters

parts.note: to rate is an old word for scold or rebuke

explanation.surface: Dangerous speeding can lead to a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of the speed word; 'rate' as rebuke is an old usage, as in being rated by a superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate acts are rash and careless of risk, so reckless.

clue.text: Stop building, house by Panamanian port

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a common British building
Colón is a port at the Caribbean end of the Panama Canal

explanation.surface: Construction halts on a house near a port in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: A SEMI (semi-detached) is a British house joined to its neighbour on one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop is an old name for a punctuation mark, and this mark makes a pause between clauses.

clue.text: Scrutinize rising young man in disgrace

parts.note: to scan is to examine closely

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: Examine an ambitious youth caught in shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns LAD into DAL in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Shameful public outrage is a synonym of disgrace.

clue.text: Smogs upset young Weller's direction

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Sam Weller in Dickens's Pickwick Papers is the son of old Tony Weller
aim is a direction

explanation.surface: Fogs upset the course of a youngster named Weller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns both pieces round together, not each alone; Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens, son of the elder Tony Weller.
explanation.definitionFit: Miasmas are noxious vapours or polluted air.

clue.text: Monarch causing dispute within the boundaries of Canton

indicators.note: within places the quarrel between the two outer letters
the boundaries are the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: a row is a dispute

explanation.surface: A king provokes conflict inside a Swiss district.
explanation.walkthrough: C and N are the first and last letters of Canton.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown stands for the sovereign by metonymy.

clue.text: Simple garment fashionable clergy look at first

indicators.note: at first puts the word for look at the front

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
in means fashionable
the cloth means the clergy

explanation.surface: Trendy priests eye a basic piece of attire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' is a traditional name for the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth is a single strip of cloth, about the simplest garment there is.

clue.text: Material stocked in many London stores

indicators.note: stocked in says the fabric is kept within the words

explanation.surface: A fabric is sold in many shops in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocked in' points inside 'many London'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic fabric used for stockings is a material.

clue.text: Stories dogging pious French king in the USA

indicators.note: dogging means following close behind, so the stories come after the king

parts.note: Louis I of France was known as Louis the Pious
ana is a collection of anecdotes or table talk

explanation.surface: Tales trail a devout French monarch across America.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis I, son of Charlemagne, was called 'the Pious'; ANA (anecdotes) follows him.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a southern state of America, named after a French king.

clue.text: College circle that's caught between opposing sides

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: caught between says the following letters sit inside the two sides

parts.note: right and left, R and L, are opposite sides
that is, Latin id est, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A college ring finds itself caught between rival factions.
explanation.walkthrough: IE (that is) sits between R and L, the two opposing sides, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Call experts to identify this writing

indicators.note: call here means say aloud, so the word for experts is pronounced

parts.note: pros are professionals, experts

explanation.surface: Summon specialists to work out who wrote a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' looks like summon, but it signals speaking: PROS said aloud gives the word for ordinary writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary written language not in verse is called prose, as these very clues are.

clue.text: The same small container is found in the West Indies

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same
mini means small
a can is a container

explanation.surface: An identical little box turns up in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the written short form of ditto.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominica and the Dominican Republic are Caribbean nations, so the adjective describes something from there.

clue.text: Flyer's complaint about a touring car

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the complaint goes round the car

parts.note: a wail is a loud complaint
GT stands for gran turismo, a touring car

explanation.surface: A pilot moans about a sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer's' reads as possessive but is 'Flyer is'; 'about' wraps the complaint round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This small songbird with a constantly bobbing tail is a flyer in the bird sense.

clue.text: Development not permitted for this inexperienced band

parts.note: green means inexperienced
a belt is a band

explanation.surface: A beginner musical group is refused permission to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: A green belt is the protected countryside ring round British towns where building is barred.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning law bars building on this protected open land around towns.

clue.text: Sounds like a certain battle call

definitions.text: Sounds like a certain battle call

parts.words: Sounds like a certain battle call
parts.note: a call to appear sounds like the Somme, the First World War battle, with 'ones' tagged on

explanation.surface: A bugle cry echoes a famous battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Somme was a major First World War battle in France; the official call begins with its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A summons is an order to appear, a formal call to court or to duty.

clue.text: Shame, to cut end off untidy facial hair

indicators.note: untidy says the letters are messed up
end off means the final letter is removed

explanation.surface: It is a shame to cut the end off scruffy whiskers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end off' trims CUT to CU, and 'untidy' rearranges SHAME TO CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grown on the upper lip is facial hair.

clue.text: Stalk about in New York displaying such harshness

parts.note: to stalk is to stride

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the city

parts.note: NY is New York
c is circa, about

explanation.surface: Walking around Manhattan shows how loud it can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives the abbreviation for circa, the usual crossword sense, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stridency is shrillness or grating loudness.

clue.text: Adverts about Oriental cigarettes

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the verb goes round the letter

parts.note: to advert to something is to refer to it
E for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: Advertisements promote Eastern smokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adverts' looks like a plural noun but is the verb advert, to refer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefers is slang for cannabis cigarettes, hand-rolled joints.

clue.text: Relentless skill in bridge

indicators.note: in places the skill inside the bridge

parts.note: a span is a bridge
art is skill

explanation.surface: Unyielding talent shown at bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' looks like the card game, but is a span.
explanation.definitionFit: A spartan regime is harsh, unrelenting.

clue.text: One confirming payment for midday courses?

explanation.surface: Someone vouches for the cost of a lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Luncheon vouchers were paper tokens British employers gave staff to pay for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: One who vouches confirms or attests, and a ticket exchanged for a meal is the same word.

clue.text: Arched flyover seen by means of the Tube

parts.note: via means by means of
a duct is a tube

explanation.surface: A bridge is visible from the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Tube' suggests the London Underground, but is a duct.
explanation.definitionFit: A viaduct is a long arched bridge over a valley.

clue.text: Play without dialogue

parts.note: a drama for a single performer has no exchange between characters

explanation.definitionFit: A dramatic piece for one actor only, so nobody to converse with.

clue.text: Low quarters for a creature that strips trees

parts.note: to low is to moo
S and E are compass quarters

explanation.surface: Lodgings for an animal that strips bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A moose is a large deer that browses on bark and shoots.

clue.text: How to court girls, some say? It's a fact

indicators.note: some say means spoken aloud

parts.note: date 'em, the way to court them

explanation.surface: A dating tip is presented as a fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date 'em' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single fact or item of information.

clue.text: Half-hearted backing for favourite American state

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
ID is the postal abbreviation for Idaho

explanation.surface: Lukewarm support for a beloved US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support, but turns PET into TEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm is a synonym, both literally of water and of enthusiasm.

clue.text: Each abandoned a musical composition

indicators.note: abandoned means the letter is dropped

parts.note: apiece means each

explanation.surface: Every individual gave up on a musical work.
explanation.walkthrough: APIECE loses A.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a single musical work.

clue.text: One's left subtle hints, that's plain

indicators.note: left means departed, so those letters go from the word

parts.note: overtones are subtle hints or implications
One's here gives the letters of ones

explanation.surface: Someone has dropped subtle hints, making the meaning obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's left' means ONES has gone, taken out of OVERTONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Open, not hidden, is a synonym for plain.

clue.text: Badly hurt once by knight's cudgel

indicators.note: badly means the letters are in a poor, jumbled order

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Someone was badly hurt by a knight's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges HURT ONCE into TRUNCHEO, then N.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer's short club is a truncheon, a kind of cudgel.

clue.text: Cafe housing explosive device in unstable state

indicators.note: in places the device inside the jumbled letters
unstable means shaken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: A café contains a bomb in a shaky condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unstable' rearranges STATE to ESTAT; 'housing' only joins, while 'in' puts the device inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French café or bar.

clue.text: Time for a sight of our opponents

explanation.surface: Time is the foe of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How goes the enemy?' is an old jocular way of asking the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang calls time the foe; and a foe or adversary in war is an opponent.
